comparisons.peer_summary: AUS includes institutional, third-party distributed, and high-net-worth client assets under discretionary management or advisory, including mutual funds, hedge funds, and separately managed accounts, but excludes self-directed brokerage assets.
comparisons.comparison: Both disclosures define the boundary of wealth management assets by explicitly distinguishing between advisor-led/managed assets and self-directed client assets. Goldman Sachs defines Assets Under Supervision (AUS) as including discretionary and advisory relationships but explicitly excludes 'self-directed brokerage assets' (gs_2024_7_P132_S005). Similarly, Morgan Stanley defines 'self-directed client assets' specifically as 'active accounts which are not advisor led' (ms_2024_7_P055_S001). While GS focuses on what is excluded from its managed asset definition and MS defines the metrics for the self-directed channel, both address the same operational distinction between managed and self-directed client assets.
